1. Introduction

1.1 Kessler State University (the “University”) is seeking proposals from qualified firms to provide custodial services for the buildings listed in Exhibit A – Buildings in Scope, located on the Main Campus, the Health Sciences Campus (2.4 miles east of the Main Campus) and the Downtown Center. The University enrolls approximately 14,200 students, of whom approximately 3,100 live on campus.

1.2 The University intends to award one contract for all buildings. Proposers shall price every building in Exhibit D; partial proposals will not be considered.

2. Contract Term

2.1 The initial contract term shall be July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028. The University may renew the contract for four (4) additional one-year periods, for a maximum of five (5) years, subject to satisfactory performance and the availability of funds.

3. Current Contract

3.1 Custodial services for the Exhibit A buildings are currently provided by Allpoint Custodial Group, LLC under Contract No. KSU-C-22-0447, awarded in 2022 for the period July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2027 (a one-year initial term and four one-year renewals). The total value of the current contract over its five-year term, including all renewals, is $26,480,000. Contract documents are available upon request under the Missouri Sunshine Law (Chapter 610, RSMo).

4. Scope Summary

4.1 The Contractor shall clean each building listed in Exhibit A on the number of service days per week shown in Column H, to APPA Level 2 (“Ordinary Tidiness”) unless the Remarks column or Exhibit B specifies APPA Level 1 for clinical and simulation spaces. Column H governs the service days for every building.

4.2 Square footages: Column D is gross square footage from the University facilities inventory and is provided for reference; Column E is cleanable square footage and is the basis for the Exhibit C staffing workbook. Buildings with zero (0) service days are listed for information only and shall not be priced.

4.3 Residence halls (Buildings 1102 Ozark Hall, 1104 Cedar Hall, 1106 Juniper Hall and 1108 Sycamore Suites): service covers common areas (lobbies, lounges, corridors, laundry rooms) and community restrooms only. Student rooms and suite bathrooms are excluded. The residence halls require service seven (7) days per week while the halls are open, and a thorough cleaning at the end and the beginning of each semester. University apartments and houses (Buildings 1110 Maple Apartments and 1120 Honors College House) are not residence halls; they are serviced on the days shown in Column H.

4.4 Hours: evening service shall be performed between 5:00 PM and 1:30 AM. Weekend service at seven-day buildings shall be performed between 7:00 AM and 3:30 PM. The Contractor shall provide day porters at the Student Union and Boreham Library from 7:00 AM to 3:30 PM, Monday through Friday.

4.5 The Contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, equipment, chemicals and consumables (paper products, hand soap and liners).

4.6 Winter conditions: from November 15 through March 15 the Contractor shall keep building entrances, vestibules and walk-off mats free of tracked-in snow, ice-melt residue and standing water. Cape Bluff averages five (5) to six (6) measurable snow or ice events per winter. Exterior walks, steps and parking lots are cleared by University Grounds staff and are not part of this contract.

5. Staffing Workbook

5.1 Proposers shall complete Exhibit C – RFP Staffing Workbook showing, for each building, the number of custodial FTEs by shift, the assumed cleanable square feet per FTE, and supervisory staffing. Staffing will be evaluated for consistency with the proposed price.

6. Proposal Submission and Evaluation

6.1 Proposals shall be submitted electronically through the University’s eProcurement portal by the due date and time. Proposals sent by e-mail or fax will not be accepted. Questions shall be submitted in writing to the Procurement Contact by the Questions Due date; answers will be issued only by addendum.

6.2 Proposals will be evaluated on the following criteria:

CriterionPoints
Cost (Exhibit D – Pricing Pages)40
Staffing Plan and Exhibit C Staffing Workbook25
Experience and References (three higher education accounts)20
Quality Control, Training and Transition Plan15
Total100

6.3 Missouri requirements: the Contractor shall enroll and participate in a federal work authorization program (E-Verify) and submit the affidavit required by Section 285.530, RSMo; and shall certify that it is not currently engaged in, and will not engage in, a boycott of goods or services from the State of Israel as required by Section 34.600, RSMo. Qualified Missouri service-disabled veteran businesses will receive the preference points provided by Section 34.074, RSMo.

6.4 The University reserves the right to reject any and all proposals, to waive minor irregularities, and to negotiate with the proposers whose proposals are reasonably susceptible of being selected for award.
